Edit: After having finished the entire first season, I've been able to observe how the show and this music video make each other better. Many of the images shown in this video reveal more about the story. We see how the firelights cherished by Powder in her youth became a weapon developed by Jinx and the namesake of Ekko's Firelights. In the show, we only get to see Vi eating at Jericho's shop after her release from Stillwater Prison, but we can see her and the rest of her adopted family eating together in their youth in this video. In the show, we only see the young Ekko as a friend of Powder's adopted family, but the portrayal of Powder and Ekko in this music video shines a brighter light on what they meant to each other in their childhood, making the meaning of their fight in Act III much deeper. This is a great example of how the art of the 21st century often manifests itself in multiple genres simultaneously, all of which build upon each other.

0:37 - We start hearing darker undertones in the music, indicating that their sweet life together will soon end because of Viego's inability to rule the country
0:52 - Return to Viego's original theme before he met Isolde, perhaps meaning she came I'll at this point and he was once again, alone
1:20 - Music intensifies, Viego is going into madness
1:31 - A sense of urgency is added, Viego gets desperate and spends all of the kingdoms resources trying to find a cure, cue in Kalista traveling the world montage
1:57 - After a spike in the sense of urgency, that feeling is quickly removed and more dread is added, Isolde has died
2:29 - After Isolde's death theme feature, once again we return to the original theme of Viego Alone
2:55 - Viego sails out to the Blessed Isles
3:04 - He attacks the Blessed Isles in order to revive Isolde, a battle
3:23 - On screen, a semi-final draft of Viego's splash art appears, signifying him choosing who he is and dooming the Blessed Isles for the sake of his love, he puts Isolde's body in the water
3:45 - The splash gains colour, Isolde became a wraith and stabbed Viego with his blade, Ruining the Isles, now we are in present day

Viego's theme is a masterpiece and actually goes very deep, it is basically telling the character's whole story musically. I'll try to explain some things with my very bad english :

-The first part is a very quick introduction : few notes played by a piano, symbolising going back in time, like if we were told a story
(kinda reminds me of zelda BOTW's scene with the king (no spoil for people that haven't played the game even tho it would only be spoiling the first hour of play))

- 00:13 Is a part that symbolizes the old kingdom's greatness (strings going crescendo, while still playing quite slowly). It is a great transition because it sets up the environnement for our story : an old majestic kingdom. Camavor's kingdom will be represented with strings fot the rest of the theme.

- 00:25 The use of the music box symbolizes Viego's wedding with Isolde ( The music box was a wedding gift lorewise). The strings fade away, but are still there, playing very quietly (we'll be going over that later). The music focuses almost entirely on the box because we are entering Viego's intimacy, his love with Isolde.

-00:49 This small transition part (approx 15sec) is absolutely godlike and goes so deep in so many different ways : the music box stops with a high pitched voice symbolizing Isolde's death as the strings rise. Those strings are again tied to the kingdom and to the conspiracy that made Isolde die "in the name of the kingdom's glory" because she was a seamstress. This is when we notice the importance of the low volume of the strings in the last part. It was symbolizing the kingdom's glory, the invisible conspiracy that was planned without Viego's knowledge right before his eyes. It was a foreshadowing to Isolde's death. We can hear a male voice few seconds after, symbolizing Viego discovering his wife's dead body after she died from poison.

-1:03 The strings slowly fade away and we are just left with viego's sadness, his desperate search for an antidote (symbolized by the piano)
We can hear his kingdom calling for him through the strings, but Viego refuses to listen to it ( you always have one high pitched note done by strings before having a musical answer by the piano (Viego's symbolized by a piano and will be for the rest of the theme) )which leads to a deeper answer from the strings, almost like a deception. The moment when the strings and the piano unite is near the end of the part, because Viego heard about the blessed isles and is ready to take the whole kingdom with him

-1:30 This part symbolizes the trip to the blessed isles, and the resulting war, we can hear Viego (the piano) communicating with the kingdom (the strings) or, by extension, his army, before uniting again for the part's final, where we hear again the female vocals, symbolizing Isolde's ressurection

-2:00 this part is obviously made to translate Viego's disappointment musically. His mental is slowly starting to break as he realizes there is no way to bring back a dead person (sike yone)


-2:20 This part symbolises time flowing, Viego has been asleep for 1000 years, but it's time for him to awaken.

-2:30 This part is a direct parallel to the first one, we are getting told a new story, except this story is about someting ancient coming back, this story is happening right now

-2:54 this part is symolizing the madness and degeneration of Viego's mind, setting up a key factor of our second story (it's a parallel to the second part aswell, which makes it even cooler : you could argue that the second part being about the old kingdom of Camavor this part could be about the shadow isles, which is absolutely genius since it would litteraly describe the shadow isles as Viego's wicked mind)

-3:03 this part is a direct reprise from the travel / war to the blessed isles but using both strings and piano in  more even proportions :
Viego is using the black mist to destroy countries. His kingdom is no more, the only way Camavor  exists now is in Viego's mind and Viego's army. He is Camavor's last sovereign and the only reminder of that old era (let's forget vladimir I don't think Viego knows he even exists). He is by extension tied to his old kingdom

-3:30 This last part just symbolizes pure madness and destruction, with both piano and strings playing very strong, impactful chords like they were explosions

Editing because people really misunderstood my comment and think I was criticizing the M/V when i'm doing the opposite:

I originally thought the animation for the "more" gesture (at 1:04 in this video) was awkward in the official M/V. But after watching the choreo, I think the animators captured it really well. I thought the movement was a bit rigid and unnatural in the m/v, but now it seems like that's just part of the actual move in real life. It's a little stiff but on purpose. Or at least, it's unavoidable as it's not a move that can really be done softly.

People don't really understand how difficult it is to model characters doing simple things like sitting or breathing, let alone dancing - let alone MULTIPLE models dancing. Watching the choreo lets me appreciate both the dancers (in real life) but also the work of the animators.

To me, this doesn't sound like the theme of a idol celebrity. It sounds like the theme of a smart, softspoken girl, who grew up working and tinkering with all sorts of strange and beautiful instruments in her parents' "hexcoustics shop". 
This sounds like she's enjoying herself while listening to all sorts of musical notes coming from things that tick like metronomes, or wind and string instruments that look like advanced Piltovan tech which we can't even begin to picture in our minds. This theme is like her harmonizing with all these instruments at once. Like she's not singing in front of a crowd, but instead singing to herself in a little shop going from instrument to instrument that have been brought by customers so she could repair them. And as she goes around the shop, adding new chords to her symphony, either fixing it with little tweaks from her tools, or playing it momentarily to get even more into the music and feel more inspired. She's alone, but she's happy that way, because she's more at peace when she doesn't have to listen to the overpowering singing of the souls of other people. That's why she likes instruments so much. 
It's wonderful. It's too bad that it's not the champion we got in the lore.

I honestly thought I would hate Seraphine when she was first revealed. I was a Sona main back when I had time to play League, and I didn't like Seraphine's whole anime-esque pop-idol aesthetic. But, as it turns out, I LOVE HER. She's got way more depth than I expected, and this song definitely reflects that. I also think her connection to the brackern and the origin of hextech is really interesting, and I definitely want to see where that goes in the future with other Piltover-centric stories in Runeterra like Arcane. Heck, even the outfit is okay -- Seraphine is literally a performer wearing a costume, and the crazy pink hair makes a LOT more sense given that we now know her family comes from Zaun. (Which also seems to be the birthplace of Runeterra's equivalent of modern music, for that matter, given the presence of the Chempunk Shredder in Legends of Runeterra.)

So, really, I think Seraphine's pretty great.

Her whole kit is literally her being a pop star. Evelynn’s a succubus, Akali is an assassin, Ahri is Vastayan, Kai’sa is a scavenger of the Void. But Seraphine is just this generic pop star. For those who want to dance to the song, break it up into session. Slow the playtime. Work with your arms first and hand movements, and repeat that segment till your familiar. Then work with your legs at the same segment, till your familiar with also the slow playspeed. Then work your work to sync both hands and legs. Once your familiar, slowly increase the playtime. Familiarize yourself then try at normal speed time. Continue this procedure with all the other segment, and hopefully just hopefully, you will learn the dance. 

 ALSO DONT FORGET TO STRETCH. PS. this is just my learning technique from a person who likes to dance casually, it may not work for everyone.

EDIT: as Choi san suggested , learn it mirror if you can. Highly suggested.

There were times where phrases could have been referenced in the choreo more. "Hearts in Twos" is the most obvious one, but there's more. "Nah not that" could have had fun diagonally crossed arm motions to resemble slashing/distaste. "Diamonds on drip cause I came to make a splash" could have had some sort of finger motions/ maybe a jump on "splash" reminiscent of a child playing in puddles. "In the cut just like a razor" should not have been punches when it would have been so much better as something like finger guns slashing in different directions. "You cover your wounds, but underneath them a million voices in your head that whisper, "Stop, now"". 
"It's all in your mind and it's fighting you". 
"It's your reflection looking back to pull you down". 
"So are you gonna die today or make it out alive, you gotta conquer the monster in your head and then you'll fly". 
"Go bury your demons then tear down the ceiling, Phoenix, fly".

It's like the song is telling me, "You'll get through this; keep going and you'll be reborn. You'll fly."

Rookie's Lissandra - 2015 World's in EU, IG finished last in their groups, defeated by FNC, AHQ, and C9(posters in the subway), one of the "easiest" groups back then. His beautiful Lissandra performance won their last game vs C9, but it was filled with desperate, regret, and shame. It was LPL's worst year ever and he received A LOT of hate comments together with every other LPL player. The "genius mid"- GodV from 1st seed LGD changed his ID then finally retired afterwards due to the never-ending storm of hate comments. It was Rookie's 1st season in the LPL and it was the start of his 3yr disappearance from the world stage - the lowest moment in his career.  
2nd theory: 2018 World's quarterfinals, 3rd game vs KT Rolster, he failed to defend the base and IG lost the game by 2 autos on the Nexus. 

Caps' Irelia - 2018 World's FNC lost to IG, he went 0-4 then 1-6 on one of his best champ Irelia, and FNC got completely destroyed in the next two games as well. We all knew how confident Caps had been in the tournament and he did flex on various midlaners before the final, so it was huge destruction for him. 

Faker's Karma - 2017 World's SKT lost to SSG, in that ardent sensor meta, he picked Karma to fully support Bang. Being 0-2 but 4 drakes ahead in game 3, there was still hope for SKT. However, in the last fight, his misposition got caught by Ruler's Varus Flash+R and lost the game, and that is one of the direct reasons why he cried at the end. Now that he is back in the spotlight again, and he knows that there's only one enemy to him - the one watching behind the media crowd. 

These are the monsters in their heads. They need to fight these bad memories to become the real King this year!

0:00-1:18 Atreus, a warrior son to battles a thousand times lost and brother to soldiers resting beneath wheat ascended Mount Targon. The weight of all his defeats heavy on his shoulder, he climbed the bitter cliffs of the mountain until even shame could not keep up with his resolve: to obtain greater power from the godly Aspects in hopes to defend his people. Reaching the top, the sky opened to a realm beyond comprehension and the Aspect of War, Pantheon, gazed through into the mortal’s soul. For centuries, those that scaled Targon’s peak deemed worthy were blessed with the Aspect’s divine powers they were welcomed with. But rather blessing Atreus with his strength, Pantheon took possession of Atreus’ mortal body as his unwilling host. On that day a man did not descend from Targon’s peak, but a god, rising as a beacon of celestial might. Pantheon’s light streaked skywards, setting the stars in his constellation ablaze as he took up spear and shield to carry out his divine and heroic deeds along with his legend. The god combed the lands for the dreaded Darkin, demonic beings forged in a bygone age, in self-imposed justice. Pantheon earned many exalted battles against them. Whether it be on land, ocean, or sky he would be there to snuff out their darkness. He felt this feat was only something he must fulfill, as it would prove too much for a disgraceful mortal like Atreus. But at the very least, his body would serve Pantheon’s godhood purpose well, basking Pantheon in the glory he's always sought for as the Aspect of War.



1:19-2:05 Pantheon faced a Darkin like none he's ever seen. One who thirsted for the top of Mount Targon that spelled danger to all other Aspects. Its heart colder and darker than the blackest corners of the arctic regions of Freljord, Aatrox. His name loathed by both mortal, and especially Aspect, earning him the title of God Killer and World Ender. Pantheon clashed with the Darkin in the skies. Their fight raged and shook the stars itself in a storm of transcendental might, leaving the Earth at their battle’s mercy. Mortals below could only find themselves swept by the two immortals' wrath as the Earth shattered. Until Aatrox fulfilled his namesake. The God Killer had slain the god. Freeing Atreus of the aspect that held his body hostage, but also robbing him of the divine powers that allowed him to protect those he cared for, leaving him nothing but a powerless shield and spear.



2:06-2:46 A band of barbarians were unfortunate enough to cross paths with Aatrox as they found themselves under siege by the Darkin’s fury months later. "Pantheon" returned to face Aatrox once again standing between them. Not as the Aspect of War, but as Atreus himself. A man who had known nothing but defeat driven by his unfettered will and resolve to protect those around him. Aatrox's unrelenting and mighty blows leave Atreus helpless and on the edge of defeat. Striking Atreus to his knees that have been all too familiar to the ground. The cries of those around him ring like a siren, urging him to stand once more as all seems hopeless. Atreus can hear all their voices rekindling not only his unyielding will but the power of the Aspect of War in both shield and spear. Their light, his light, was shimmering. Just like that of Pantheon's rise. 



2:47-3:31 Atreus yelled with his returned godly might clashing his spear and shield against the World Ender's greatsword sending magnificent sparks and flares that put the heaven's light to shame. Aatrox in the heat of battle is completely taken aback by Atreus' returned surge of power that felt even greater from that of Pantheon. No... it wasn't that Atreus was stronger. It was that the Aspect's weapons were inflamed by the unimaginable will of a mortal to fight off death itself. Heavier than Atreus’ spear was the weight of fulfilling one life no god could match. With a celestial leap, Atreus came streaking down like a comet with his spear blazing. Severing the Darkin's arm as he fell to his knees with his demonic blade. For the first time, Atreus was, at last, the final man standing. This time as a mortal over a god killer. The god may have died, but the man that is Atreus lives. He was now a new Pantheon.

My thoughts about this.

Art: at the bottom, you can see Morgana is holding her arms up (palms upwards), and she appears to be crying. Meanwhile, Kayle is at the top, with a valiant look.

This could mean two things. One, since Morgana has already been traumatised by their father's death, she is further saddened that the both of them have to fight due to different ideals (Kayle upholds justice, Morgana upholds leniency). This is supported by the fact that she chained her wings in an attempt to forget her divinity after witnessing her father's death. Two, Kayle has placed her task of upholding justice above everything else, including the care of her own sister, Morgana.

Song: 
[Beginning (only voices, before the strings)]
The soprano and alto refers to the mood of Morgana and Kayle respectively (for this part). Considering Morgana has suffered a lot, the soprano sings her pain and grief. For Kayle, she still has some, otherwise a few, human emotions, hence the alto is singing with regards to Kayle's possible regrets, for continuing the uphold of justice, until either one - Kayle or Morgana - wins.

[After beginning until 2:12]
Elaboration on grief.

[2:12]
You can tell that the key of the song changed into something darker. Before this, it was like telling the story of grief. Between 2:12 and 3:12, the melody of the song suddenly indicated regret.

[3:13]
The song gets darker, as if this regret spoken between 2:12 and 3:12 was disregarded, and this person being depicted is now persistent on achieving their goal(s).

[3:41]
The song gets even more dramatic with the bass now emphasised. This points to hostility - preparing to fight someone.

Basically, the beginning was about Morgana, and the middle to end was about Kayle.

In summary, or tl;dr, this song, along with the splash art, suggests that Kayle is classified as lawful neutral under the D&D alignment. This is because she only cares about order and justice and nothing else. Morgana, on the other hand, is classified as chaotic good, as she goes against unjust laws to allow for change amongst those who repent for their crimes. Kayle does not like this, and sees it as Morgana going against her.

In other words, sister issues. However, while Morgana loves Kayle very much, it does not apply the other way round, which suggests why Kayle, in game, mostly refers to Morgana as "sister" instead of "Morgana".
